issues: Cool grey with grey skeleton bars on the phone screen: you couldn't tell what the product was, and every frame looked like a wireframe
The phone was cropped at both top and bottom, so the subject was never complete
The two chips carried placeholder copy ("Feature one / Feature detail"), small and without icons
No brand and no landing point, so the last frame wasn't a finished poster
changes: Look switched to sand: four warm sand concentric discs (the outer two bleed off-frame) with lit top edges and hairline rims, plus a warm-white glow behind the phone; the out-of-phase breathing (±6%, 1.7 rad, 1.5 cycles) is kept

The phone is rebuilt at native 1080p size: 430×900, fully in frame (83% of frame height), with a warm titanium frame, dynamic island, side buttons, glass reflection and three tinted contact shadows; it rises into place from below over the first 26f

The screen is a podcast app designed for the shot, "Murmur": large title, featured card, episode cards with geometric cover art and listening progress, and a persistent mini-player whose progress advances and waveform moves; the feed auto-scrolls at constant speed

The chips now name real features, "Offline listening / Smart chapters": 36px text with a terracotta icon disc, a single-overshoot spring pop (damping 13) sliding out from the phone's edge, with the ±8px float easing in only after they land, left and right 1s apart
A wordmark "Murmur — Podcasts, unhurried." rises word by word bottom-left at 90f, so the shot ends on a product poster
